description:
FILED s521 (Fable, 2026-10-18 18:5x) from the ROUND-2 BOARD on MAIN-READY-34 (review/board-r2.log: LOST Data-Dump-1.25-0 glob.t 1 passing row, 6 -> 5) and its attribution: t/glob.t passes 6/6 on the ed8a4504 extraction (MAIN-READY-32), 5/6 on 0b836815 (-33 = s521a) and on main -- so s521a's **#3433** (a glob ref carries its bless class ON THE GLOB through the table filehandles already use).

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 / base ed8a4504 / main 81afe6b0; scratchpad rv/globstr3.pl):
    use Symbol qw(gensym); use IO::Socket::INET;
    sub via_arg { my $rval = \$_[0]; return "" . $$rval }      # Data::Dump's inner _dump shape (Dump.pm:254 `_dump($$rval, ...)`, :261 `"$$rval"`)
    my $g = bless gensym(), 'X';
    print via_arg($$g), "\n";          # perl *Symbol::GEN0   base *Symbol::GEN0   main X=*Symbol::GEN0
    print "" . *$g, "\n";              # perl *Symbol::GEN0   base same            main *Symbol::GEN0  (the DIRECT spelling is right)
    my $s = IO::Socket::INET->new(Listen => 1, LocalAddr => '127.0.0.1');
    print via_arg($$s), "\n";          # perl *Symbol::GEN1   main IO::Socket::INET=*Symbol::GEN1
perl's rule: the GLOB VALUE stringifies as `*PKG::NAME` always; only the REFERENCE to a blessed glob stringifies as `Class=GLOB(0x...)`.  Since #3433 the class lives on the glob object, and the stringifier reached through the @_ alias slot (`\$_[0]` -> `$$rval` -> to-string of what the slot holds) prints `Class=` + the glob name -- a glob VALUE must never show a class (rule: the class belongs to `ref` / the reference's string, not to the glob's own name).  The direct spelling `"" . *$g` is right, so the arg-slot path reaches a different stringifier (grep the glob to-string arms in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp: the one that formats `Class=` for a blessed referent vs the glob-name one; the @_ slot holds the glob object itself, not a box).

WHERE IT BITES: Data::Dump of any blessed glob object (IO::Socket, IO::Handle, IO::File, FileHandle): Data-Dump t/glob.t row 5 (`my $a = bless(Symbol::gensym(), "IO::Socket::INET")` expected); the blessed row cites this task; it LEAVES by edit when fixed (one-file run `tools/run-dist-t.pl --rows ~/.cpan/build/Data-Dump-1.25-0 t/glob.t` = 6/0).

FIX: in the s521d batch (member 0, before #3492 -- the same file, a regression on main takes precedence).  Probe vs perl BEFORE and AFTER the four lines above + `"$$g"` inside a sub taking the glob, `*{$g}` through a sub, a blessed named glob `\*FOO` through @_ (#3491's family: say what it does), `local *FH` blessed; the #3433 guard (`Pl/t/bless-referent-01.t` t12) must keep passing (re-bless through a COPY still reaches the glob) -- the fix is in the glob VALUE's stringification, not in where the class lives.  Guard row in bless-referent-01.t (the via-@_ glob string), inverse FAILS on main; a `cl/` change: the sweep.
subject: REGRESSION since MAIN-READY-33 (s521a #3433): a GLOB VALUE passed through @_ and read back via \$_[0] stringifies WITH its bless class (`X=*Symbol::GEN0`) where perl prints the glob itself (`*Symbol::GEN0`) -- Data::Dump renders a blessed IO::Socket::INET as `bless(\IO::Socket::INET=*Symbol::GEN1, ...)` instead of `bless(Symbol::gensym(), ...)`; Data-Dump t/glob.t row 5 LOST (6 -> 5); PRIORITY: a regression on main
